source_observations.quote: At today's review BP 174/102 mmHg was followed after rest by BP 158/92 mmHg, and he says he missed a blood-pressure tablet that morning. There is no documented persistent reading, no verified four-week period of control and no recent specialist report; the nurse records possible glucose-related symptoms and variable pressure measurements without assigning a definite cause or choosing one reading as representative.
source_observations.explanation: The note explicitly states the observed diastolic blood pressure as 102 mmHg.

source_observations.quote: The driver reports diabetes managed with tablets, but an older specialist letter describes diet and exercise alone and the current medication box is not available for verification; he says the tablets were changed last month and has not used insulin to his knowledge. During a late shift he became shaky and struggled to read a docket, then ate a snack without assistance and felt better, but no glucose was checked until nearly an hour later, when the meter displayed 6.2 mmol/L.
source_observations.explanation: The driver reports diabetes managed with tablets.
